An interactive introduction teaches movement, captures, and enemy replies. Discover all six chess pieces and inspect their reach whenever you need a closer look. These are original puzzle rules inspired by chess, not a traditional chess match.

KEEP YOUR MIND MOVING
Play 20 introductory puzzles, then continue through endless generated challenges. Every board has a solution without tools. Earn up to three stars, retry for free, and return to improve your best result.

A LITTLE ADVENTURE EVERY DAY
Try the daily puzzle, collect daily gifts, and spend earned coins on optional hints and tools. Share your achievements and compare progress through optional Game Center leaderboards.

PLAY YOUR WAY

newReleases.name: Case 16: Murder Sudoku
newReleases.desc:
A murder, a floor plan, and a clue from every suspect.

Put each suspect on the square where they stood: one to a row, one to a column. The victim was alone with the killer, so whoever shares their room did it. No guessing, no luck — every case has exactly one answer, and you can reach it by reasoning alone.

THE RULES FIT ON A CARD
• One suspect to every row and every column.
• "Beside" means left, right, above or below — never diagonal, never through a wall.
• Nobody stands on furniture. Tables, plants and boxes are solid; chairs, beds and carpets are somewhere to be.
• The victim was alone with the killer. Their room holds exactly two people.

80 CASES, EASIEST FIRST
From a 5×5 warm-up to 12×12 boards that take a whole evening. Bars, ferries, hospitals, film sets, a reading of the will. Every difficulty is measured from the steps it takes to solve, not guessed, so the case number is the ladder.

A NEW CAST EVERY CASE
Suspects are dealt fresh for each case — different faces, clothes, hats and habits — so you are never solving the same five people twice.

THE MONTHLY CASE
Once a month, one big 12×12 case and one attempt. Fastest times go on the ranking.

HINTS THAT TEACH
Stuck? A hint shows the next step of the deduction and why it follows — never just the answer.

FAIR ABOUT ADS

Ant Laboratory is a living ant colony to watch, and a laboratory to study it in. Release one queen into a glass ant farm, watch her colony grow, then follow it out across an island of its own.

Begin with one queen
Choose from six species: black garden, fire, wood, leafcutter, carpenter and harvester ants, each with its own nest, diet and habits. Pick one of six soils for the farm; only the look changes. Release the queen and watch the first workers emerge (the wood ant's solo start is Experimental). Every ant in the farm is simulated: nurses feed larvae, diggers carve tunnels and rooms, foragers follow scent trails and undertakers clear away the dead. Follow one worker close up with the Ant cam.

A living ant farm
Tap Habitat to set the light, the water and the warmth. Choose Bright, Soft or Off, any colour, or up to twice as bright. The mister can water the soil by itself, and a heat mat can hold the warmth. Mould grows where it is damp, tiny springtails graze it, and the ants catch them. Over weeks the bare surface turns green with algae, moss and grass (how fast is Experimental). Keep the soil too dry or too wet for days, or the heat mat too hot, and some brood dies. Adult ants are never harmed by the habitat.

An automatic feeder keeps the colony fed. Tap Feed to offer seeds, sugar, a fly or a cricket, and follow the food home.

Keep it, or let it out

newReleases.name: Woodpile: Sort Puzzle
newReleases.desc:
Woodpile is a sorting puzzle that waits for you.

A woodpile seen end-on: round log ends packed into a small hex lattice, each one wearing a painted colour mark the way a forester marks timber. Three stacks sit under the pile. Drag one onto any free cell and the pile sorts itself - neighbouring stacks with the same colour on top slide together, and when ten of a kind sit together they are carted off. That is the entire rule set.

A PUZZLE THAT DOES NOT HURRY YOU

No timer. No move limit. No energy meter, no lives, no daily login reward. Put the phone down mid-thought and the pile is exactly where you left it. Nothing in Woodpile is built to pull you back - it is built to be worth coming back to.

THE PILE DOES THE SORTING

You only decide where a stack goes. Everything after that is the pile's own logic, played out in front of you: a merge exposes a new colour, which matches another neighbour, which fills a run to ten, which clears and exposes the next. The satisfying part of a good move is watching how far it travels.

TODAY'S PILE

One pile a day, dealt from the date itself, identical for everyone who plays it. There is no server and no account - the stacks are worked out from today's number on your own device, so it works on a plane.

Three years ago, the gnomes shattered the northern line of defense, led their mechanical army into the fray. Thousands of cities fall and the fate of human kind hangs in the balance. Now Immortals are gathering under your banner. The greatest ones in history are now ready to lead your fearsome troops into battle! Lords! Would you able to repel enemies and restore peace to this scarred land? 

Help! Them Gnomes are wreaking havoc!
You have finally arrived, my Lord! Our territory is in dire situation! The Gnomes have ransacked our cities like a plague of locusts, and our people desperately need your help! The alchemists are ready to help us restore the City, so that the people can come to seek refuge. Rebuild the city, grow faster, build faster, train faster, and then put it all on the line against those enemies! 

Immortals Assemble!
There are more than 50 powerful Immortals from various civilizations ready to the aid of humanity. The Sage Council grants you the supreme right to summon the Immortals at the Hall of Immortals via  Philosopher's Stone. With their immensely powerful abilities, Immortals will fight for your cause. Cleopatra, Julius Caesar, Merlin, Robin Hood…Your troops have been assembled! They are ready to fight for you to expel
